name: regulation and standards
owns: the rules that decide what is permitted, what must be disclosed, what must be kept, and what a system is legally obliged to do under attack
why_in_D: This lens is not an attack category and yet it changes what is possible. It decides whether a test is a crime, whether a company must publish a breach, how long it must keep evidence, and which controls a payment processor will accept as sufficient. A technical control that regulation does not recognise is a control with no enforcement behind it.

factors.name: authorisation scope of a test
factors.def: whether the permission covers the exact host, method and data touched
factors.observable: a test action outside the written scope

factors.name: written authorisation existence
factors.def: whether permission exists in writing and names the parties
factors.observable: an action with no document behind it

factors.name: third party hosting in scope
factors.def: whether a SaaS or cloud provider's own terms permit the test
factors.observable: a test against infrastructure the customer does not own

factors.name: data handling obligation during a test
factors.def: what must happen to data encountered, and how quickly
factors.observable: customer data retained after the engagement

factors.name: unauthorised access statute breadth
factors.def: how broadly the local computer misuse law reads, which decides whether a proof is itself an offence
factors.observable: an action that exceeds the statute's allowance

factors.name: good faith defence availability
factors.def: whether the jurisdiction recognises a research defence at all
factors.observable: a prosecution brought despite disclosure

factors.name: disclosure deadline
factors.def: the time allowed to report a breach once known
factors.observable: days between knowledge and notification

factors.name: notification recipient set
factors.def: who must be told: regulator, data subjects, partners, payment schemes
factors.observable: a required recipient omitted

factors.name: breach definition threshold
factors.def: what counts as a reportable breach versus an incident
factors.observable: an incident classified below the threshold without a recorded reason

factors.name: cross border transfer restriction
factors.def: whether data may leave the jurisdiction, which decides where logs and backups may live
factors.observable: a record stored outside a permitted region

factors.name: data subject access obligation
factors.def: whether a person can demand their data, and whether the system can produce it
factors.observable: an access request the system cannot answer

factors.name: erasure obligation feasibility
factors.def: whether data can actually be deleted from backups, logs, caches and third parties
factors.observable: a record surviving an erasure request

factors.name: retention limit conflict
factors.def: whether a retention requirement conflicts with a minimisation duty
factors.observable: data kept past the shorter of the two obligations

factors.name: legal hold override of deletion
factors.def: whether a preservation order suspends deletion and whether the system honours it
factors.observable: a deletion performed during a hold

factors.name: consent record completeness
factors.def: whether consent is recorded with time, version and scope
factors.observable: a processing action with no consent record

factors.name: consent withdrawal propagation
factors.def: whether withdrawal stops processing everywhere, including downstream
factors.observable: processing continuing after withdrawal

factors.name: legitimate interest assessment
factors.def: whether a processing basis other than consent is documented and defensible
factors.observable: processing with no documented basis

factors.name: payment card data scope
factors.def: whether card data enters the environment at all, which decides the whole compliance burden
factors.observable: a card number present in a store or log

factors.name: tokenisation coverage
factors.def: whether the system holds tokens rather than numbers, everywhere and always
factors.observable: a path holding a real number

factors.name: cardholder data environment boundary
factors.def: whether the boundary is drawn accurately or assumed
factors.observable: a system inside the boundary treated as outside

factors.name: health data identification risk
factors.def: whether a dataset can be reidentified by combination
factors.observable: an individual isolated from deidentified data

factors.name: children's data constraints
factors.def: whether age verification exists and what it costs in data
factors.observable: processing without an age basis

factors.name: financial record keeping
factors.def: whether transactions are recorded to the standard a regulator would expect
factors.observable: a transaction with no durable record

factors.name: audit log integrity obligation
factors.def: whether logs are tamper evident as regulation may require
factors.observable: an editable audit record

factors.name: standard interpretation divergence
factors.def: whether two auditors reading the same standard reach different requirements
factors.observable: a control accepted by one and rejected by another

factors.name: standard version drift
factors.def: which version of a standard the claim of compliance refers to
factors.observable: a compliance claim with no version attached

factors.name: certification scope
factors.def: whether the certificate covers the system in question or only a sibling
factors.observable: a certificate applied to an uncertified system

factors.name: assessor independence
factors.def: whether the party auditing was paid by the party audited
factors.observable: an assessment with no independence

factors.name: self attestation weight
factors.def: whether compliance rests on a questionnaire the organisation filled in itself
factors.observable: a control with no external verification

factors.name: cryptographic export control
factors.def: whether the jurisdiction restricts the algorithm or its distribution
factors.observable: a deployment using a restricted primitive

factors.name: lawful interception capability
factors.def: whether the system can be compelled to produce data, and whether that path is authenticated
factors.observable: a data release without dual control

factors.name: subpoena versus warrant distinction
factors.def: whether the organisation applies different verification to different legal instruments
factors.observable: a request honoured without the higher instrument

factors.name: transparency report obligation
factors.def: whether requests received must be disclosed in aggregate
factors.observable: a request with no record in any report

factors.name: sanctions and export screening
factors.def: whether a user or payment can be checked against a list
factors.observable: service provided to a sanctioned party

factors.name: accessibility obligation as availability
factors.def: whether an accessibility requirement is also a denial of service surface
factors.observable: a mechanism enabling abuse of a legitimate feature

factors.name: platform terms as a control
factors.def: whether a cloud provider's acceptable use policy forbids the test
factors.observable: a test blocked by provider policy rather than technology

factors.name: insurance requirement
factors.def: which controls an insurer requires before covering an incident
factors.observable: a gap between the control set and the policy

factors.name: contractual security obligations
factors.def: what a customer contract promises, which becomes a legal exposure if untrue
factors.observable: a marketing claim contradicted by the control set

factors.name: service level as a security claim
factors.def: whether an uptime commitment creates pressure to avoid taking a system down when compromised
factors.observable: a compromised service kept online to meet an SLA

factors.name: right to explanation
factors.def: whether an automated decision must be explainable to the person affected
factors.observable: a decision with no recorded rationale

factors.name: automated decision restriction
factors.def: whether a decision may be made without human involvement
factors.observable: a consequential decision made automatically

factors.name: profiling disclosure
factors.def: whether profiling is disclosed and whether an opt out exists
factors.observable: profiling with no notice

factors.name: vendor contract security schedule
factors.def: whether the supplier is contractually required to notify and to cooperate
factors.observable: an incident at a supplier with no notification duty

factors.name: data processing agreement coverage
factors.def: whether every processor is covered by an agreement
factors.observable: a processor with no agreement

factors.name: onward transfer restriction
factors.def: whether a processor may engage another processor without consent
factors.observable: a fourth party with no recorded approval

factors.name: disclosure of a vulnerability before patch
factors.def: whether the organisation can embargo and for how long
factors.observable: a disclosure published before a fix shipped

factors.name: bug bounty legal terms
factors.def: whether the program grants a licence to test and a promise not to sue
factors.observable: a researcher exposed to legal risk after a good faith test

factors.name: terms of service wording breadth
factors.def: whether a prohibition is wide enough to criminalise ordinary use
factors.observable: a normal action forbidden by terms

factors.name: digital signature legal weight
factors.def: whether an electronic signature is binding in the jurisdiction
factors.observable: an agreement that may be unenforceable

factors.name: record retention for evidence
factors.def: whether logs meet the standard for evidentiary use
factors.observable: a log that would not survive challenge

factors.name: chain of custody practice
factors.def: whether captured evidence records who handled it and when
factors.observable: an artefact with no provenance

factors.name: jurisdiction of the data subject
factors.def: whether the law that applies depends on the user's location rather than the server's
factors.observable: a user in a stricter jurisdiction handled under a weaker rule

factors.name: cross border law enforcement request
factors.def: whether a foreign request is handled through the proper channel
factors.observable: a foreign request honoured directly

factors.name: sector specific incident reporting
factors.def: whether a sector regulator has a shorter deadline than the general one
factors.observable: a report filed late against the sector rule

factors.name: critical infrastructure designation
factors.def: whether the system is designated, which raises every obligation
factors.observable: a designated system treated as ordinary

factors.name: supply chain due diligence duty
factors.def: whether the organisation must assess its suppliers by law
factors.observable: a supplier never assessed

factors.name: vulnerability reporting to a regulator
factors.def: whether exploitation must be reported even without data loss
factors.observable: an exploited flaw unreported

factors.name: open source licence obligation on distribution
factors.def: whether shipping a binary triggers a source disclosure duty
factors.observable: a distributed artefact with unmet licence terms

factors.name: trademark and impersonation remedy
factors.def: whether a lookalike domain can be acted against and how fast
factors.observable: a lookalike with no takedown attempt

factors.name: regulator technical competence
factors.def: whether the notifying body can evaluate the report, which changes what must be explained
factors.observable: a report that required translation into non technical terms

factors.name: liability allocation with a supplier
factors.def: who pays when a supplier's flaw causes a breach
factors.observable: an incident with no contractual recovery

factors.name: standard conflict resolution
factors.def: what happens when two applicable standards demand incompatible things
factors.observable: non compliance with one by complying with the other

factors.name: documentation obligation as exposure
factors.def: whether required documentation itself reveals detail an attacker would want
factors.observable: architecture detail in a filing or public register

factors.name: enforcement precedent direction
factors.def: whether recent enforcement in the jurisdiction is widening or narrowing
factors.observable: a practice lawful last year and not this year
